title: Mission Control · ESCAPADE slingshots to Mars

post.title: Two NASA probes just slingshotted past Earth toward Mars 🔴
post.description:
NASA's twin ESCAPADE spacecraft launched in November 2025, when Mars was on the far side of the Sun. Instead of waiting on the ground, they spent a year looping around a point about 1.6 million km from Earth, then came back. On 7 and 9 November 2026 each one swept past Earth (the second at about 1,000 km) and fired its engine for about 9 minutes to head for Mars. Arrival is planned for 7 and 9 September 2027, when they'll fly in formation to study how the solar wind strips Mars's atmosphere.

Source:
NASA Science, NASA's ESCAPADE Completes Powered Earth Flybys, Now En Route to Mars: https://science.nasa.gov/science-research/heliophysics/nasas-escapade-completes-powered-earth-flybys-now-en-route-to-mars/

Images: NASA / KSC / Blue Origin (launch, 13 Nov 2025), NASA / KSC / Kim Shiflett (the ESCAPADE spacecraft), NASA / JPL / USGS (Mars, Viking). Narration uses a synthetic voice.

narration: Two NASA spacecraft just slingshotted past Earth, on their way to Mars.
They launched a year ago, when Mars was on the far side of the Sun.
So instead of heading straight there, they waited in space, looping around a point about 1.6 million kilometres from Earth.
On the 7th and 9th of November, each one swept past Earth, the second as low as about 1,000 kilometres, and fired its engine for about nine minutes.

params.label: above Earth at closest, then a 9-minute engine burn

narration: Now they're cruising for 10 months, due at Mars on the 7th and 9th of September, 2027.
There they'll fly in formation, to study how the solar wind strips away Mars's atmosphere.
It will be the first science mission to choreograph two orbiters around Mars.

params.label: the first science mission to fly two in formation at Mars
